key_insight: DFT predicts stronger vacancy association in CrN than TiN, with compact mixed-vacancy clusters remaining stabilised at CrN surfaces but becoming unfavourable at TiN surfaces.
engineering_relevance: Coating defect-control strategies should account for material-specific chemical potentials, vacancy clustering, and depth-dependent stability rather than bulk energetics alone.
method: Compare native vacancies in rocksalt TiN and CrN using DFT.
Evaluate bulk and (001) surface energetics within phase-stability-constrained chemical potentials.
Reference association energies to isolated vacancies, using preferred vacancy depths for surface comparisons.
evidence_signal: For compact two-metal/two-nitrogen vacancy clusters, association energies change from +0.217 to −0.346 eV per vacancy from bulk to surface in TiN, versus +1.188 to +0.431 eV in CrN; positive values indicate favourable association.
watch_item: The abstract reports energetic preferences, not finite-temperature vacancy populations or migration kinetics, so processing outcomes require further validation.
paper_title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
